title: Audio Guide to the Imperfections of a Perfect Masterpiece

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: For the last several months, I've been working on something with the Guggenheim Museum in New York.
sentences.zh: 过去几个月里，我一直在与纽约古根海姆博物馆合作一个项目。

sentences.en: It's a brand new audio tour about the history and design of a truly great work of American architecture.
sentences.zh: 这是一个全新的语音导览，讲述了一座真正伟大的美国建筑杰作的历史与设计。

sentences.en: Even if you've never been to the Guggenheim, you probably recognize it.
sentences.zh: 即使你从未去过古根海姆，你也可能认得它。

sentences.en: From the outside, the building is a light gray spiral.
sentences.zh: 从外观上看，这座建筑是一个浅灰色的螺旋体。

sentences.en: And inside, the art is displayed on one long ramp that curves up towards a glass skylight in the ceiling.
sentences.zh: 而在内部，艺术品沿着一条长长的坡道展示，坡道向上蜿蜒，直通天花板上的玻璃天窗。

sentences.en: There is no museum like it, and it was made by one of my favorite architects, Frank Lloyd Wright.
sentences.zh: 没有哪座博物馆像它这样，它出自我最喜欢的建筑师之一，弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特之手。

sentences.en: What you're going to hear now is the whole audio tour.
sentences.zh: 接下来你将听到的是完整的语音导览。

sentences.en: If you're in New York City, you should try and listen to it inside the museum.
sentences.zh: 如果你身在纽约，不妨试着在博物馆内聆听。

sentences.en: There are signs on every floor indicating where you should stop.
sentences.zh: 每一层楼都有标识，提示你应该在哪里驻足。

sentences.en: But if you can't make it to New York, the tour is still really fun and works on its own.
sentences.zh: 但如果你无法前往纽约，这个导览依然非常有趣，单独听也完全没问题。

sentences.en: The team at the Guggenheim were generous enough to allow me to create a different kind of audio tour
sentences.zh: 古根海姆的团队非常慷慨，允许我创作一种与众不同的语音导览，

sentences.en: that feels like walking through the building with an extremely enthusiastic and knowledgeable friend
sentences.zh: 让你感觉就像是在一位极其热情且博学的朋友陪伴下参观这座建筑，

sentences.en: rather than a formal architecture professor.
sentences.zh: 而不是在听一位刻板的建筑学教授讲课。

sentences.en: I hope you like it.
sentences.zh: 希望你会喜欢。

sentences.en: We're going to post an episode guide with photos on our website at 99pi.org
sentences.zh: 我们会在网站 99pi.org 上发布带有照片的剧集指南，

sentences.en: so you can follow along at home.
sentences.zh: 这样你在家也能跟着导览走。

sentences.en: But I think you can close your eyes and imagine and still enjoy all the stories.
sentences.zh: 但我认为即使闭上眼睛去想象，你依然能享受所有的故事。

sentences.en: Here's the first stop.
sentences.zh: 这是第一站。

sentences.en: If you're in the building, start playing this in the lobby of the Rotunda.
sentences.zh: 如果你就在馆内，请在圆形大厅的入口处开始播放。

sentences.en: Welcome to the Guggenheim Museum.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到古根海姆博物馆。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars, the creator and host of the Design and Architecture podcast, 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯，设计与建筑播客《99%隐形》的创作者兼主持人。

sentences.en: The Guggenheim Museum is an architectural masterpiece made by a master of architecture, Frank Lloyd Wright.
sentences.zh: 古根海姆博物馆是由建筑大师弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特打造的建筑杰作。

sentences.en: In 2019, UNESCO selected eight buildings designed by Wright, including the Guggenheim,
sentences.zh: 2019年，联合国教科文组织将赖特设计的八座建筑（包括古根海姆）选为，

sentences.en: to be a World Heritage Site.
sentences.zh: 世界遗产。

sentences.en: UNESCO sites are considered vital to the collective interests of humanity.
sentences.zh: 世界遗产被认为对全人类的共同利益至关重要。

sentences.en: Yellowstone is a heritage site.
sentences.zh: 黄石公园是世界遗产。

sentences.en: So is the Grand Canyon.
sentences.zh: 大峡谷也是。

sentences.en: Of the World Heritage properties in America, 12 were made by God.
sentences.zh: 在美国的世界遗产中，有12处是上帝的杰作。

sentences.en: Eight were made by Frank Lloyd Wright.
sentences.zh: 有8处是弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特的杰作。

sentences.en: When co-founder and first director of the Guggenheim Museum,
sentences.zh: 当古根海姆博物馆的联合创始人兼首任馆长，

sentences.en: Hilla Rebe, commissioned this building,
sentences.zh: 希拉·雷贝委托设计这座建筑时，

sentences.en: she said she wanted a temple of spirit, and Wright designed one for her.
sentences.zh: 她说她想要一座精神殿堂，而赖特为她设计了一座。

sentences.en: Here's the director of the Guggenheim, Richard Armstrong.
sentences.zh: 下面是古根海姆博物馆馆长理查德·阿姆斯特朗。

sentences.en: I feel now when I look up into that dome, I'm actually looking at a very beautiful abstraction of a rose window in a cathedral.
sentences.zh: 我现在抬头望向那个穹顶时，感觉自己看到的实际上是大教堂玫瑰窗的一种非常美丽的抽象表达。

sentences.en: I'm in awe.
sentences.zh: 我心怀敬畏。

sentences.en: So we're going to take the genius of this building as a given.
sentences.zh: 我们就把这座建筑的天才设计视为理所当然吧。

sentences.en: It's great.
sentences.zh: 它确实很棒。

sentences.en: What I'm going to focus on are the oddities, the accretions, the interventions that reveal a different kind of genius.
sentences.zh: 我将重点关注那些奇特之处、增建部分以及各种干预措施，它们揭示了另一种天才。

sentences.en: Not just the genius of Frank Lloyd Wright and his bold, original vision,
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特及其大胆、原创愿景的天才，

sentences.en: but the genius of all the people that made this building function, adapt, and grow over the decades.
sentences.zh: 更是几十年来让这座建筑得以运作、适应并不断成长的人们的天才。

sentences.en: Frank Lloyd Wright was the originator of a concept called organic architecture.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特是“有机建筑”这一概念的创始人。

sentences.en: And you might look around and see how this entire building resembles a seashell,
sentences.zh: 你环顾四周，可能会觉得整座建筑看起来像个贝壳，

sentences.en: and you might think, oh cool, well that must be organic architecture.
sentences.zh: 你可能会想，哦，真酷，那这一定就是有机建筑了。

sentences.en: But sorry, that's actually not what he meant.
sentences.zh: 但抱歉，那其实并不是他的本意。

sentences.en: Really, for Frank Lloyd Wright, organic architecture was more about the metaphor of a living organism.
sentences.zh: 实际上，对弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特而言，有机建筑更多是指生物有机体的隐喻。

sentences.en: This is Ashley Mendelsohn, the Guggenheim's assistant curator of architecture and digital initiatives.
sentences.zh: 这位是阿什利·门德尔松，古根海姆博物馆建筑与数字计划助理策展人。

sentences.en: And actually, when he was on the site, he referred to the steel as the tendons and the muscles of the building,
sentences.zh: 事实上，当他在现场时，他将钢材比作建筑的肌腱和肌肉，

sentences.en: the concrete as the fatty tissue, and the waterproof paint as the skin.
sentences.zh: 将混凝土比作脂肪组织，将防水漆比作皮肤。

sentences.en: So we're going to explore, touch, and even dance with this living organism of a building
sentences.zh: 所以，我们将去探索、触摸，甚至与这座充满生命力的建筑共舞，

sentences.en: and witness the evolution that's occurred within these curved walls.
sentences.zh: 并见证这些弧形墙壁内所发生的演变。

sentences.en: The next stop is by the second floor elevators on the main ramp.
sentences.zh: 下一站是主坡道二楼的电梯旁。

sentences.en: Frank Lloyd Wright's plan was for the Guggenheim to be a top-down museum.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特原本计划将古根海姆建成一座自上而下的博物馆。

sentences.en: Originally, visitors were supposed to ride the elevator to the top of the spiral ramp and walk down.
sentences.zh: 最初，参观者应该乘坐电梯到达螺旋坡道的顶部，然后步行向下参观。

sentences.en: That's where the exhibitions all started.
sentences.zh: 展览都是从那里开始的。

sentences.en: I've seen many images of old installation views from the 60s into the 70s,
sentences.zh: 我见过许多60年代到70年代的旧展览现场照片，

sentences.en: where that's where the intro text was.
sentences.zh: 展览的导言文字就是放在那里的。

sentences.en: Initially, the exhibitions were planned from top-down, starting on ramp 5.
sentences.zh: 起初，展览规划是从上往下，从5号坡道开始。

sentences.en: Get out of the elevator.
sentences.zh: 走出电梯。

sentences.en: The entrance name of the exhibition was right in front of you, and you walked down to see it.
sentences.zh: 展览的入口名称就在你面前，你走下去就能看到。

sentences.en: But over time, curators started programming from the bottom up.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，策展人开始从下往上进行规划。

sentences.en: It just felt natural.
sentences.zh: 这感觉很自然。

sentences.en: Also, the Guggenheim does a lot of retrospectives, focusing on one artist, from their early work to the late stuff.
sentences.zh: 此外，古根海姆经常举办回顾展，聚焦于某一位艺术家，展示他们从早期到晚期的作品。

sentences.en: Many artists, over the course of their careers, their work got larger in scale.
sentences.zh: 许多艺术家的作品在职业生涯中规模变得越来越大。

sentences.en: And so if you're doing a retrospective where you're starting with the early work, which is small,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你举办一场从早期小件作品开始的回顾展，

sentences.en: and then moving to larger work, it makes sense to start at the bottom,
sentences.zh: 然后过渡到大型作品，从底部开始参观是有道理的，

sentences.en: because the display spaces in the building get bigger and bigger as you move up in space.
sentences.zh: 因为随着空间向上延伸，建筑内的展示空间也变得越来越大。

sentences.en: But if you want to be a Frank Lloyd Wright originalist, and you really need to walk down from the top of the Guggenheim,
sentences.zh: 但如果你想成为一名弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特的纯粹主义者，非要从古根海姆的顶部走下来，

sentences.en: you might have company as you ride up the elevator.
sentences.zh: 那你坐电梯上去时可能会有同伴。

sentences.en: I think still 15 to 20% of people take the elevator up.
sentences.zh: 我想目前仍有15%到20%的人会选择坐电梯上去。

sentences.en: And it's probably because they heard that that's how Frank Lloyd Wright intended, and they want to see it that way.
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为他们听说这是弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特原本的意图，他们想以那种方式参观。

sentences.en: And so most designers and curators plan for it to be experienced both ways.
sentences.zh: 因此，大多数设计师和策展人在规划时，都会考虑到两种参观方式。

sentences.en: And in fact, most visitors that I talk to walk up and then walk down.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我交谈过的大多数参观者都是先走上去，再走下来。

sentences.en: So it makes sense that the show should be able to read in both ways.
sentences.zh: 所以，展览能够以两种方式解读是有道理的。

sentences.en: This isn't the only big difference from how Frank Lloyd Wright envisioned the Guggenheim.
sentences.zh: 这并不是弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特构想的古根海姆博物馆与现实之间唯一的巨大差异。

sentences.en: His blueprints included plans for a second spiral ramp that would protrude out into the center of the rotunda.
sentences.zh: 他的蓝图中包含了一个第二螺旋坡道的计划，该坡道会向圆形大厅中心凸出。

sentences.en: It was going to be twice as steep as the corkscrew ramp you are standing on right now.
sentences.zh: 它将比你现在站着的这条螺旋坡道陡峭两倍。

sentences.en: He called it the quick ramp, and it was supposed to make it faster to get between floors.
sentences.zh: 他称之为“快速坡道”，本意是让楼层间的通行更加快捷。

sentences.en: And Frank Lloyd Wright, in the description, said,
sentences.zh: 弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特在描述中曾说：

sentences.en: Feel the pull of gravity as you walk down the grand ramp,
sentences.zh: 当你走下宏伟的坡道时，感受重力的牵引，

sentences.en: and for quick and easy access between ramps, take the quick ramp, which is really good.
sentences.zh: 若想在坡道间快速轻松地穿行，就走“快速坡道”，那真的很棒。

sentences.en: But on the quick ramp, you'd feel gravity's pull a little too much.
sentences.zh: 但在“快速坡道”上，你会感受到过强的重力牵引。

sentences.en: The design was way too steep.
sentences.zh: 那个设计实在太陡了。

sentences.en: It was more like a quick slide.
sentences.zh: 与其说是坡道，不如说更像是个快速滑梯。

sentences.en: So it never got built.
sentences.zh: 所以它最终没能建成。

sentences.en: But the quick ramp still influenced the final design of the museum.
sentences.zh: 但“快速坡道”依然影响了博物馆的最终设计。

sentences.en: You'll notice the hole in the center of the rotunda, it's not a perfect circle.
sentences.zh: 你会注意到圆形大厅中心的那个洞，它并不是一个完美的圆。

sentences.en: And the ramp you're on right now is not a perfect spiral.
sentences.zh: 而你现在所处的坡道也不是一个完美的螺旋。

sentences.en: There's a semicircle that juts out into the rotunda.
sentences.zh: 有一个半圆形结构向圆形大厅内凸出。

sentences.en: That's called the bump out.
sentences.zh: 那被称为“凸出部”。

sentences.en: The bump out used to be part of the quick ramp.
sentences.zh: 这个凸出部曾经是“快速坡道”的一部分。

sentences.en: When you see that, then you understand that every curve actually belongs to a circle somewhere.
sentences.zh: 当你看到它时，就会明白每一条曲线其实都归属于某个圆。

sentences.en: They all had a reason for being there.
sentences.zh: 它们的存在都有其缘由。

sentences.en: Sadly, we missed out on the opportunity to slide our way down the Guggenheim.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，我们错失了在古根海姆博物馆里滑行而下的机会。

sentences.en: But the stairs we got as an alternative route between floors are still pretty delightful.
sentences.zh: 但作为楼层间替代路线的楼梯，依然非常迷人。

sentences.en: You can find them in the hallways behind the elevator doors.
sentences.zh: 你可以在电梯门后的走廊里找到它们。

sentences.en: They twist up the building in a triangle and add another lovely, pure form to the museum.
sentences.zh: 它们在建筑内呈三角形盘旋而上，为博物馆增添了另一种优美、纯粹的形态。

sentences.en: The next stop is by the third floor elevators on the main ramp.
sentences.zh: 下一站位于主坡道的三楼电梯旁。

sentences.en: As you walk up the ramp in the rotunda, place your hand on the parapet.
sentences.zh: 当你沿着圆形大厅的坡道向上走时，把手放在栏杆上。

sentences.en: That's the low wall separating the ramp from the void in the center.
sentences.zh: 那是将坡道与中心虚空隔开的矮墙。

sentences.en: The first thing you'll notice is that it's very low.
sentences.zh: 你首先会注意到它非常低。

sentences.en: If it were built today, let's be honest, it would probably be a couple inches taller.
sentences.zh: 老实说，如果是在今天建造，它可能会再高出几英寸。

sentences.en: The other thing you'll notice is that even though the building is composed of these pure forms like circles and spirals,
sentences.zh: 你还会注意到，尽管这座建筑由圆形和螺旋等纯粹形式构成，

sentences.en: the top of the parapet isn't perfectly rounded or finished off with a crisp right angle.
sentences.zh: 但栏杆的顶部并非完美圆润，也没有以利落的直角收尾。

sentences.en: It's bumpy and uneven.
sentences.zh: 它凹凸不平，参差不齐。

sentences.en: So the reason why the parapet is kind of lumpy in that way is because we touch up paint truly every day when the museum's not open,
sentences.zh: 栏杆之所以呈现出这种凹凸感，是因为博物馆闭馆时，我们确实每天都在修补油漆，

sentences.en: and that's because the building's white, and so it gets dirty.
sentences.zh: 这是因为建筑是白色的，所以很容易变脏。

sentences.en: You'd have to really close the whole building and have it closed for, you know, I don't know, a full week or something
sentences.zh: 如果你想彻底重新粉刷室内，你得真正关闭整座建筑，停业，你知道，我不知道，大概整整一周左右，

sentences.en: if you were to truly repaint the interior.
sentences.zh: 才能完成这项工作。

sentences.en: And so instead, we touch up here and there, and for that reason, everything kind of has a texture.
sentences.zh: 所以我们选择随处修补，正因如此，一切都带上了一种质感。

sentences.en: You have an effect on this building.
sentences.zh: 你对这座建筑产生了影响。

sentences.en: By being here and touching this railing, you've changed it.
sentences.zh: 因为你的到来并触摸这道栏杆，你已经改变了它。

sentences.en: Its changing texture is part of its evolution as an organic structure.
sentences.zh: 它不断变化的质感，正是其作为有机结构演变的一部分。

sentences.en: Okay, stay right here.
sentences.zh: 好了，就待在这里。

sentences.en: This is the second stop on the third floor.
sentences.zh: 这是三楼的第二站。

sentences.en: Constructing Frank Lloyd Wright's vision of a spiral museum was not an easy feat to pull off.
sentences.zh: 构建弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特心目中的螺旋博物馆并非易事。

sentences.en: Wright oversaw the work, but a local architect named William Short was in charge of the project on the ground,
sentences.zh: 赖特监督了这项工作，但一位名叫威廉·肖特的当地建筑师负责现场项目，

sentences.en: and George Cohen was the general contractor.
sentences.zh: 而乔治·科恩则是总承包商。

sentences.en: In the three years it took to build the Guggenheim,
sentences.zh: 在古根海姆博物馆建造的三年来，

sentences.en: they came to the realization that some of Wright's ideas were not going to be doable,
sentences.zh: 他们意识到赖特的一些想法是无法实现的，

sentences.en: like the idea of making the building a self-supporting spiral.
sentences.zh: 比如将建筑设计成自支撑螺旋的想法。

sentences.en: If you imagine a slinky or something in the way that the wire,
sentences.zh: 如果你想象一下弹簧玩具之类的东西，那种金属丝，

sentences.en: just because it's in tension in that way, is holding itself together,
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为它处于那种张力状态，就能自我支撑，

sentences.en: that's what he said early on.
sentences.zh: 这就是他早期的设想。

sentences.en: So instead of a self-supporting spiral, they use something called web walls.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们没有使用自支撑螺旋，而是使用了所谓的“腹板墙”。

sentences.en: Look at the floor across from you.
sentences.zh: 看看你对面的地板。

sentences.en: Those thin walls that you see that jut out from floor to ceiling,
sentences.zh: 你看到的那些从地面延伸到天花板的薄墙，

sentences.en: those are actually all connected.
sentences.zh: 其实它们都是连接在一起的。

sentences.en: Those are the web walls.
sentences.zh: 那些就是腹板墙。

sentences.en: They hold this whole building together.
sentences.zh: 它们支撑着整座建筑。

sentences.en: These vertical walls, which extend all the way up into the oculus,
sentences.zh: 这些垂直墙体一直延伸到顶部的天窗，

sentences.en: the combination of all of those together is the structural skeleton of the building.
sentences.zh: 所有这些墙体的结合构成了建筑的结构骨架。

sentences.en: Everything else hangs off of it.
sentences.zh: 其他一切都悬挂在它上面。

sentences.en: The ramp hangs off of it.
sentences.zh: 坡道悬挂在它上面。

sentences.en: The exterior walls hang off of it.
sentences.zh: 外墙也悬挂在它上面。

sentences.en: They had to solve the problem of making a curving spiral building
sentences.zh: 他们必须解决建造一座弯曲螺旋建筑的难题，

sentences.en: no one had even imagined before, much less built.
sentences.zh: 这是前人从未想象过，更不用说建造过的。

sentences.en: And they did it with Gunite.
sentences.zh: 他们用喷射混凝土完成了这项工作。
